Jensen Huang's return as chief executive of Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) sent shares of its Asian partners and suppliers sharply higher on Tuesday.

Asian Markets Rally as US Futures Hold Gains

S&P 500 futures edged up 14.25 points, or 0.20%, to 7,268.75 as of around 7:42 p.m. EST on Monday. The Nasdaq 100 futures climbed 1,751.75 points, or 6.97%, to 26,878.25, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average futures rose 1,447.98 points, or 3%, to 49,595.31.

In Asia, South Korea's KOSPI jumped 5.81%, to 4,982.20, while Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed 3.56%, to 58,446.83 in early Tuesday trade.

Memory Makers and AI Partners Lead Gains

Nvidia's key memory suppliers led the gains, with SK Hynix Inc.'s (NASDAQ:SKHY) Seoul-listed shares jumping 8.02% to KRW 1.17 million ($870.86), and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. rising 6.82% to KRW 189,600 ($140.95).

In Tokyo, SoftBank Group Corp. gained 4% to JPY 3,146 ($19.78), while Fujitsu Ltd. climbed 1.71% to JPY 3,389 ($21.32).

NVDA Board Reverses Course on Jensen Huang

Just 12 days after accepting Huang's resignation, Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as CEO.

The board said senior U.S. government officials gave input and that it is confident his return poses no national security risk.

Price Action: Nvidia closed 31.48% higher on Monday at $165.05 and climbed 1.05% in after-hours trading at $166.79.

title: If a Stock Market Crash Is Coming, Warren Buffett Says This Is the Best Move Investors Should Make
detail:
If a Stock Market Crash Is Coming, Warren Buffett Says This Is the Best Move Investors Should Make
Adam Spatacco, The Motley Fool

NVDA

^IXIC

Despite stubborn inflation, rising interest rates, geopolitical conflicts, and considerable economic uncertainty, the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC), Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC), and Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) have delivered impressive returns over the last four years. However, this rapid appreciation of stocks has also raised concerns that a bubble could be forming.

Those fears are intensifying as artificial intelligence (AI) stocks retreat from record highs. Both the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 recently entered correction territory, although both indexes are rebounding sharply as Jensen Huang returns to the CEO position of Nvidia.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Fortunately, legendary investor Warren Buffett has a simple strategy for navigating periods of market turbulence.

Image source: Getty Images.

The stock market rally has created concerns about a bubble

Between Nov. 30, 2022 -- the day ChatGPT was launched to the public -- and Nov. 20, 2026, the S&P 500 advanced approximately 69%, equivalent to an annualized gain of roughly 14%. The Nasdaq performed even better, climbing roughly 97%, or 18% annually.

Much of this growth was driven by the AI revolution. Companies designing AI chips, providing cloud infrastructure, and building enterprise software have attracted outsize interest from growth investors. Meanwhile, demand for data centers is creating opportunities throughout the economy. Utilities, energy producers, industrial equipment manufacturers, and construction companies are increasingly benefiting from the infrastructure spending required to support AI adoption.

However, enthusiasm surrounding AI is also pushing stock market valuations toward historically expensive levels. One revealing indicator is the Shiller cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio, which measures the S&P 500's price relative to its average inflation-adjusted earnings over the last 10 years.

Unlike a traditional price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, CAPE readings smooth out short-term fluctuations in earnings. This makes it useful for assessing long-term valuations. Historically, the metric has averaged 17.7, meaning investors have generally paid around $18 for every dollar of normalized earnings.

Shiller CAPE Ratio data by YCharts

Currently, the CAPE ratio sits around 41 -- dangerously close to its highest level in history. That places valuations at more than twice their historical average and well above the threshold that has occasionally preceded major market drawdowns.

title: Dow, Nasdaq and Bitcoin Jump on Huang's Return, but Why Did Bitcoin Reverse?
detail:
Dow, Nasdaq and Bitcoin Jump on Huang's Return, but Why Did Bitcoin Reverse?
Darryn Pollock
Mon, November 23, 2026 at 7:00 PM MST 2 min read
BTC-USD
^IXIC
NVDA
^GSPC
MU
Trade BTC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bitcoin (BTC) touched $64,446 after Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang on Monday. It then reversed back to about $61,200 while the Nasdaq kept a 6.5% gain.

CoinGecko data shows Bitcoin ended the round trip up only 0.7% over 24 hours, while Nvidia soared 31%. Buyers near the peak now sit about 5% underwater.

Why Did Wall Street Keep Its Gains and Bitcoin Did Not?

Nvidia's board reinstated Huang on Monday after his resignation earlier this month.

President Donald Trump told CNBC he persuaded directors to make the move.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 3.01% at 49,595.31, according to CNBC. The S&P 500 gained 4.73% and the Nasdaq Composite 6.51%, each its best session since April 2025.

AI suppliers rose in sympathy, with Micron Technology up 19% and cloud provider CoreWeave up 22%.

In contrast, Bitcoin had no comparable company-level fix, so its link to the news appeared to run only through risk appetite.

Did a Short Squeeze Cause the Bitcoin Reversal?
BTC spiked and then dropped basically back to where it was. Source: CoinGecko

CoinGecko's 24-hour chart shows a near-vertical jump followed by a slide. That shape is typical of a short squeeze. In a squeeze, exchanges force-close losing bearish bets by buying, which lifts price until the forced buying ends.

However, little fresh demand appeared to hold the move once that buying faded. The read could be wrong if spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) data for Monday shows net inflows.

Still, BTIG, a Wall Street brokerage, is cautious on stocks. In a Sunday note, chief market technician Jonathan Krinsky saw only a short S&P 500 bounce toward 7,250 to 7,350. He expects a turn lower after that.

Meanwhile, the S&P 500 closed Monday at 7,237.17. US exchanges shut Thursday for Thanksgiving and end Friday's session at 1 p.m. ET.

As a result, Bitcoin trades through both with its own leverage and fund flows setting the near-term Bitcoin price outlook.

U.S. stocks made a comeback on Monday, with Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO boosting financial markets after Friday's sell-off plunged the S&P 500 and Dow into correction territory.

The Nasdaq Composite jumped 1,472 points, or 6.5%, to close at 24,090, regaining ground after the tech-heavy index on Nov. 20 suffered its second-worst day of 2026. The S&P 500 rose 4.7%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 3%.

Huang resigned less than two weeks ago amid scandal over an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies suspected of spying for China. On Monday, the board said it believes Huang is the "right person to lead Nvidia" and that it has "every confidence" in him as he resumes his leadership role at the company. Huang's reinstatement is "effective immediately," the board said.

"The company reported fantastic numbers last week, but the uncertainty of their leadership was like a huge overhang," eToro investment analyst Bret Kenwell told CBS News.

"Now that uncertainty suddenly is not only removed, but it's replaced with the very familiar leadership of Jensen," he added.

Nvidia shares surged more than 31% on Monday, adding roughly $1 trillion to its market value. Shares of CoreWeave, a cloud computing company and Nvidia customer, shot up 22%. The PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index, which tracks 30 of the largest companies involved in the design, distribution, manufacture and sale of chips, rose 14%.

"I believe the White House leaned hard on the board, and the message is crystal clear. America needs Jensen Huang leading Nvidia and, therefore, the wider AI industry," Nigel Green, CEO of investment advisory firm deVere Group, said in an email. "His return hands him more control than ever. He's got the backing of the board, the U.S. president and the market, and that's a phenomenal platform to take Nvidia to another level."

Not out of the woods

Despite Monday's market exuberance, some Wall Street analysts said investors remain on edge amid concerns that the artificial intelligence sector is unraveling.

"Stocks in the U.S. are staging a large rebound rally so far this morning, although, just to put things into context, the S&P futures aren't even reclaiming their loss from Friday, much less the entire week," Vital Knowledge analyst Adam Crisafulli said in a note to investors on Monday before Nvidia announced it was reinstating Huang.

"Sentiment remains pretty bleak — most people are looking at this [Monday] uptick as nothing more than technical in nature, a partial reversal of extremely oversold conditions," he added.

Demand is not the hard part for Cummins (CMI) Power Systems. Shipping is. The unit grew revenue 16.5% in fiscal 2025, while the rest of Cummins shrank 5.2%.

In fiscal Q3 2026, supply chain limits held back Power Systems shipments. The company's power generation sales fell short of management's own expectations. Over the month to November 20, 2026, Cummins stock lost 21.9%, against a 9.7% drop for the S&P 500. If one Cummins shareholder sent the Power Systems team a note this week, it would be short.

Cummins stock lost 21.9% in a single month, while the S&P 500 fell 9.7%. If Cummins makes up a large share of your savings, a second drop like that would take a big bite out of your nest egg. In a free 30-minute review, our partner advisory firm can show you ways to limit your loss if the stock falls further and to sell with a smaller tax bill. Book the free review.

Cummins Owners Want Power Systems To Ship Faster

The note would ask Power Systems for one thing: ship the orders held back in the third quarter. You brought in 22.2% of Cummins revenue in fiscal 2025. You are also the fastest-growing large part of the company. Your revenue reached $7.46 billion in fiscal 2025, up 16.5%. The rest of Cummins slipped to $26.2 billion, from $27.7 billion a year earlier.

In fiscal Q3 2026 you set a record. Revenue hit $2.3 billion, up 15% from a year earlier. The supply chain remains a key limit as new capacity comes online, management said on the November 5, 2026 call. The company expects to largely catch up the delayed shipments in the fourth quarter. Owners are counting on you to do it.

How Cummins Pays For The Power Systems Build-Out

Cummins is paying for the extra capacity out of the cash it already makes. Free cash flow, what is left after capital spending, came to $3.46 billion over the twelve months to September 30, 2026. Management plans capital investments of $1.35 billion to $1.45 billion across all of Cummins in 2026.

One recent piece is a plant in Somers, Wisconsin, that makes cooling systems for generator sets. It cost about $100 million. Cummins still aims to return about 50% of its operating cash flow to shareholders. The weaker side is debt. Cummins carried $8.12 billion of debt against $4.18 billion of cash at September 30, 2026. Management still called its balance sheet strong on the November 5 call.

Power Systems Has Orders Stretching Into 2028

Orders for the company's larger generator sets now reach into the second half of 2028, management said. Cummins also has contracts with some of its big hyperscaler customers, the largest data center buyers. Those contracts run past its firm orders. So buyers are lining up well ahead of what the factories can make.

title: Is Lockheed Martin Stock Ready For A Delayed Jet Contract?

Lockheed Martin (LMT) and the Pentagon struck an initial deal on October 22, 2026, to produce 850 F-35 jets. The same day, management trimmed its 2026 outlook for Aeronautics, the unit that builds the jet, citing later contract awards. Management said the deal sets a path to 850 U.S. jets over 10 years. But the contracts for the next lots are now expected later. A longer wait would fall on Lockheed Martin's largest business. It would also test holders of a stock that returned 23.5% over the past year, against 5.3% for the S&P 500. What has the later F-35 timing already cost?

Lockheed Martin Already Expects Later F-35 Contracts

Management has already built a later signing into its own numbers. On the fiscal Q3 2026 call, it guided Aeronautics to 2026 sales of $31.1 billion to $32.5 billion. That is slightly lower than its July guidance, and management tied the change to later award timing for the next F-35 lots.

Lockheed Martin expects up to $32.5 billion of sales from its aircraft unit in 2026, and its next F-35 contracts are now expected later. If you count on the shares for steady cash, a longer wait could mean a fall in the stock to sit through. The Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's, from 50 companies that have paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row. See what it pays.

F-35 Lot 20 is not in the guide at all. Management said a Lot 20 signing in 2026 would lift almost every one of its 2026 figures. Work on it is already well underway, using advance funding.

How Much Of Lockheed Martin Comes From Aeronautics?

Aeronautics brought in $30.6 billion in fiscal 2025, out of $75.0 billion for the whole company. It also builds the C-130 and the F-16, so not all of that is the F-35. For 2026, management expects Aeronautics to earn $2.92 billion to $2.95 billion. That is about a third of the $8.57 billion to $8.68 billion in segment profit it guides for the whole company.

So far, the later timing has cost Aeronautics a trim to its outlook, not its growth. Management still sees the unit's sales growing in 2026. It also said F-35 production adds to the margins of Aeronautics and of Lockheed Martin as a whole. A longer delay would therefore hold back some of the company's better-paying work.

Holders have sat through falls deeper than the market's before. During the 2023 bond yield shock, Lockheed Martin stock fell as much as 12.0% from its peak, against 9.5% for the S&P 500.

Update, Nov 23: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Nov 22. In Monday morning trading, after that news, Nvidia stock rose more than 30% and Lam rose about 15%. This article's figures are at the Nov 20 close. At about $211, Lam is still roughly 50% below its June 30 high.

Lam Research (LRCX) stock fell 39.9% from May 22 to November 20, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 7.0%. One of its sharpest one-day falls came on October 22, the day after its September-quarter report. That day, fears about AI spending returned after Lam's report, and chip stocks fell across the board. So did Lam's business shrink, or did buyers simply pay less for it?

Lam Research fell 39.9% in six months, far more than the S&P 500. If Lam is a big part of your savings, another drop like that would hurt, and selling shares bought years ago can mean paying tax on the gains. In a free 30-minute review, our partner advisory firm can show you ways to limit your loss if the stock falls further and to sell with a smaller tax bill. Book the free review.

Lam Research Earned More While Buyers Paid Less

Lam's profits kept growing while its shares fell. Net income was $8.45 billion over the four quarters to September 27, 2026, up from $5.81 billion a year earlier. So buyers now pay far less for each dollar of those earnings than they did in June. The stock trades at 27.1 times them, against 20.8 for the S&P 500.

In June, buyers paid much more. After rising from their May 22 level, the shares closed at $433.33 on June 30, their highest close of the past year. On that date the stock traded at 74.6 times its earnings over the previous four quarters. That was its highest multiple at any of the 40 quarter ends in our data, which start in fiscal Q2 2017. By November 20 the shares had closed at $183.27, about 58% below their June 30 high.

Lam did not fall alone. Its peer KLA lost 32.6% over the same dates, so buyers marked down the whole group of chip-tool makers. Applied Materials lost 29.8% and Teradyne lost 42.8% in that window. The October 22 session alone took 11.8% off Lam's stock.

What Lam Research's December Forecast Changes

Management's forecast for the December quarter is a much smaller step up than the one just reported. On its October 21 call, Lam guided to revenue of $8.6 billion, plus or minus $400 million. September-quarter revenue had been $8.22 billion, up 22% from the quarter before.

Part of that slower step is timing. Management said the guide would have been a bit higher without near-term supply chain constraints. Shipments that slip out of December because of timing are expected to go out in the March quarter.
